name: The Inlaks Residency at Skowhegan (2027)
location: Madison / Skowhegan, Maine (campus at 39 Art School Road, Madison, ME 04950)
duration: 5 June to 7 August 2027, nine weeks. Full attendance is mandatory: "Every participant must commit to being on campus for the full nine-week session." One scheduled Visitor Weekend in the first week of July allows up to three days off campus.

provides.grant: Inlaks grant covers Skowhegan tuition (USD 6,000 for 2027) plus a travel and materials subsidy paid directly to the artist. Inlaks: "The residency cost will include a subsidy for travel and material expenses for the Artist recipient, to be paid over and above the cost of tuition directly to the artist". Skowhegan separately is need-blind: "In the past decade, more than 95% of participants have received full scholarships."
provides.stipend: No living stipend. Inlaks provides a "materials stipend for 1000 USD" and Skowhegan covers all meals and lodging as part of tuition. No spending money beyond that.
provides.housing: Included in tuition. Inlaks: "Accommodation at Skowhegan, including housing and all meals." Skowhegan: "Participants live in communal lakeside cottages, and they have single and double rooms that are charming, but modest... All the bathrooms are shared." No central heating or air conditioning. Linens and blankets are provided for international participants.
provides.airfare: Inlaks: "Travel expenses will include a return ticket for the artist up to 1200 USD". Skowhegan also states: "We provide grants toward travel expenses for our international applicants."
provides.accommodation: Three meals a day in the Gund Dining Hall, included in tuition. Communal cottage dorms, single and double rooms, shared bathrooms.
provides.workspace: PRIVATE. "Each studio is approximately 10 feet by 13 feet in size. They are private, although they are all located in communal buildings." Open 24 hours a day. Shared fabrication facilities: Acquavella Sculpture Shop (wood and metal tools, spray booth), Pollock-Krasner Ceramic Studio, Moffett-Gober Sculpture Pavilion for outdoor work at scale, sewing room, Double Bet(y)(e) Media Lab with large-format printer, Flex Space, Looker Family Fresco Studio, Robert Lehman Library.
provides.artist_fee: None. No fee is paid for the work itself.
provides.materials: USD 1,000 materials stipend from Inlaks, paid directly to the artist.

application_requirements.bio: Not confirmed. Skowhegan's public page does not list a bio or CV requirement; the full question set sits behind the applicant login at application2027.skowheganart.org.
application_requirements.website: Not confirmed. Not listed on the public page.
application_requirements.portfolio: "In general, we request 10 images or 6 minutes of video of your work, accompanied by explanations to facilitate context, and two references." Plus, since 2025, "a brief video narrative introducing yourself and sharing your interests as an artist." Two references are named contacts only: "We do not require letters of recommendation." Skowhegan may contact them if the application reaches the final round.
application_requirements.artwork_details: Images or video must be "accompanied by explanations to facilitate context". Applicants also choose a practice category: "2D: painting, drawing, printmaking / 3D: sculpture, installation / Photography / Time-Based / Performance/Live Art / Social Practice/Ecological Art", and "this does not determine or restrict what they do on campus".
application_requirements.image_count: 10 images OR 6 minutes of video. Plus one separate short video narrative introducing yourself (no stated length limit).
application_requirements.image_video_format: Not confirmed. No file format, pixel or file-size limits are published on skowheganart.org/school/; specifications appear inside the logged-in application at application2027.skowheganart.org.
application_requirements.submission_method: Online only via https://application2027.skowheganart.org/ (create an account, then log in). "Our application is entirely online. Please do not send any application materials via email or physical mail." Fee paid at submission via Stripe. There is no separate Inlaks form: the Inlaks page's own Apply Now button links to skowheganart.org/school/. Applications open 1 September 2026 and close 16 October 2026, 23:59 ET. "Applications submitted after midnight of the final deadline will not be considered."
questions: As part of the application, we will ask you to consider what you can reasonably contribute towards tuition
other: TWO-STEP PROCESS, STEP 1 (fee waiver, do this first): email help@skowheganart.org BEFORE submitting. Skowhegan: "We have an agreement with Inklas Foundation in which we can waive the application fee for Indian artists younger than 35 who are living in India. Before submitting your application, please send us an email at help@skowheganart.org... Proof of nationality, residency and age will be required to waive the fee." Inlaks: "All Indian applicants who meet the Inlaks eligibility criteria should contact Skowhegan before submitting their applications, and Skowhegan will be able to waive the application fee accordingly."

TWO-STEP PROCESS, STEP 2: submit the full Skowhegan application at application2027.skowheganart.org. The Inlaks grant follows acceptance: "The applicant must be accepted to Skowhegan's summer program." No evidence of a separate Inlaks application form for this award.
Application fee: USD 25, rising to USD 50 for the final two days of the period. Nonrefundable under all circumstances. Processed by Stripe.

Inlaks eligibility: "The applicant must be an Indian passport holding citizen and resident in India at the time of application", "The applicant must be 35 years or younger in the year of application". Exclusion: "The applicant should not have received any prior grant from the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation for any other overseas project".
Skowhegan minimum age: "You must be at least 21 years of age by the start of the program. There is no maximum age."
One application per cycle. Results notified about three months after close, roughly January. About 80 candidates get an interview; 60 to 65 are invited.

Visas: "We are unable to assist with the application for a Visa or cover the associated expenses, but we can provide a letter of invitation upon request... The majority of our international participants come to Skowhegan on a tourist visa."
Language: "The common language at Skowhegan is English."
No social media permitted during the nine weeks. Nothing may be left behind: "You should also leave your studio completely empty" and installations must be removed.
Help desk: help@skowheganart.org, +1 (646) 681-6426, Monday to Friday 10:00 to 16:00 ET.

contact_email: help@skowheganart.org (Skowhegan applications and fee waiver); gladys@inlaksfoundation.org (Inlaks queries)
unconfirmed: How long the fee-waiver email takes to be processed: no turnaround time is stated on skowheganart.org/school/ or on the Inlaks page. Ask help@skowheganart.org directly and allow buffer before 16 October.

Exact form of proof accepted for nationality, residency and age: the page says only "Proof of nationality, residency and age will be required" without naming documents (skowheganart.org/school/, FAQ).
The full list of written questions and word limits: the application form is behind a login at application2027.skowheganart.org, which returns only an authentication screen.
Image and video file formats, pixel dimensions and file-size limits: not published on skowheganart.org/school/.
Whether a CV, artist statement, short bio or website URL is required: not listed on skowheganart.org/school/.
Length limit for the required video narrative: not stated on skowheganart.org/school/.
Exact value of the Inlaks travel grant versus Skowhegan's own international travel grant, and whether they stack: neither page says.

name: Alaska AIR 2027-28, Bunnell Street Arts Center
location: Homer, Alaska (106 W. Bunnell Ave, Homer, AK 99603)
duration: Generally one month per residency. Bunnell's own page: "Residencies of generally one month are scheduled in fall, winter and spring months of 2027 and 2028." The CaFE listing gives the window two ways: "generally scheduled for one month, October to April" in the summary and "generally scheduled October through May" in the residency information. Exact dates are set later: "Residency scheduling and program design is done in consultation with Bunnell's Artistic Director." Applicants state "Preferred months of residency".
theme: No single named theme. The call asks applicants to address "pertinent themes": "These may include themes such as accessibility, inclusion, sustainability, stewardship, skills sharing and exchange, connection, joy, and enhancing community well-being."

provides.grant: "One to four fully-funded Alaska AIR residencies are awarded annually. Additional or partially-funded residencies may be awarded as funding and scheduling permit."
provides.stipend: "$2000 stipend for 1 month residency (pro-rated if shorter)".
provides.housing: "Lodging in a private room with private bath, shared kitchen and living area in an apartment above the Arts Center or elsewhere in the Old Town neighborhood."
provides.airfare: "Round trip travel to Homer (up to $1000 value)".
provides.accommodation: No board. "occasional meals/food provided, shared kitchen; restaurants and grocery stores nearby (walking distance)." Wireless internet. A bicycle is available for use.
provides.workspace: SHARED and public, not private. "The residency studio is Bunnell's spacious 1000 sq foot main exhibition gallery, open to the public during regular gallery hours Monday-Saturday." Equipment on site: piano; sound system (mixer, monitors, mains, mics, cables); light board and theater lights; HD/3D video projector, HD video camera, darkroom (no enlarger), tripod; nipping press, small printing press; workshop furniture.
provides.artist_fee: Not confirmed. No separate fee for the work itself is named on the CaFE listing or bunnellarts.org; the $2000 is described as a stipend.

application_requirements.bio: Not required as a bio. A resume is required.
application_requirements.website: Not confirmed. Not listed as a requirement on the CaFE listing or bunnellarts.org.
application_requirements.portfolio: "Work samples may be images, audio, video, or a combination thereof. Up to 5 work samples may be images. Up to 3 work samples may be audio. (Total audio time should be no more than 15 minutes) Up to 3 work samples may be video. (Total video time should be no more than 15 minutes)" and "Writers may include up to 10 pages of written work as a PDF." CaFE enforces a minimum: "the Alaska AIR application on CaFE will require a minimum of 3 work samples of audio/video/image." CaFE media counts for this call: Images min 0 max 5, Audio min 0 max 3, Video min 0 max 3, Total min 3 max 5.
application_requirements.artwork_details: Not itemised in the call text beyond the work-sample counts. CaFE collects title, year, medium and dimensions per sample as standard fields. No references are requested.
application_requirements.image_count: Up to 5 images. Minimum 3 work samples in total across image, audio and video.
application_requirements.image_video_format: Set by CaFE, not by Bunnell. Images: "JPEG or JPG only", "1200 pixels or greater on the longest side", file size "under 5 MB". Audio: "AIFF, WAV, XMF, MP3", bit rate "minimum 96 kpbs-maximum 320 kbps", file size "under 10 MB". Video: "3GP, WMV, AVI, MOV, ASF, MPG, MP4, M2T, MKV, M2TS", resolution "minimum 640 x 480, maximum 1920 x 1080", bit rate "recommended above 240 kbps", frame rate "minimum 12 fps, recommended 30 fps", file size "under 100 MB". Bunnell's own caps are on duration, 15 minutes total audio and 15 minutes total video.
application_requirements.submission_method: Online through CaFE (callforentry.org). Bunnell: "Apply to this opportunity at www.callforentry.org from September 1 - October 15, 2026." Submission limit: 1. Application fee USD 25, "Needs-based Waivers available. Please email adele@bunnellarts.org to request a waiver of application fees."
questions: A statement of intent and residency proposal.
Preferred months of residency and any special needs.
other: Judging guidance, quoted: "The strongest Alaska AIR applications show a clear and unified body of work. The artist's work and intentions are clearly represented and described. The project proposal is clear, specific, and demonstrates a strong community engagement component that seeks to strengthen the social, physical and economic fabric of Homer."
Residency obligations: "Alaska AIR artists generally provide (1) an introductory artist talk or presentation, and (2) a community engagement component".
Eligibility: "Open to International, US, and Alaska artists". CaFE location eligibility type is listed as Unspecified. Eligible applicant type: Artist.
Jury: "prior artists in residence, community members, and Bunnell staff and board". Notification: "Applicants are notified by December 31."
The open call runs in alternate years: "OPEN CALL SEPT 1 - OCT 15, alternate years".
Applicant questions go to Artistic Director Asia Freeman, asia@bunnellarts.org; fee-waiver requests to adele@bunnellarts.org.
No word limits are published for the artist statement, statement of intent or proposal.

contact_email: info@bunnellarts.org (general); asia@bunnellarts.org (applicant questions, Artistic Director); adele@bunnellarts.org (fee waiver)
application_url: https://www.callforentry.org/ (Alaska AIR - Bunnell Arts 2027-2028 Artist in Residence Program; listing mirror at https://opportunities.wearecreativewest.org/opportunity/17982/CAFE)
unconfirmed: Exact residency start and end dates: only "generally one month" within fall, winter and spring of 2027 and 2028 is given on bunnellarts.org and the CaFE listing; scheduling is agreed with the Artistic Director after selection.
Word or character limits for the artist statement, statement of intent and proposal: not stated on the CaFE listing or bunnellarts.org.
Whether a website URL or references are requested: not listed on either page.
Whether the $2000 includes any artist fee for the work itself: not distinguished on the CaFE listing or bunnellarts.org.
Visa support for an Indian passport holder: neither bunnellarts.org nor the CaFE listing mentions visas or invitation letters.
Conflict in the published season window: the CaFE summary says "October to April" while the residency information on the same page says "October through May". Confirm with Bunnell.
The direct CaFE call URL could not be opened; the full call text was read from the official Creative West / CaFE listing mirror at opportunities.wearecreativewest.org/opportunity/17982/CAFE.

name: Shigaraki Ceramic Cultural Park (SCCP) Artist-in-Residence, Open-Call Guest Artist 2027
location: Shigaraki, Koka City, Shiga Prefecture (2188-7 Chokushi, Shigaraki-cho, Koka City, Shiga 529-1804)
duration: Residency window 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028. "Applicants can choose their residency period between minimum of 2 months and less than 1 year during the above-mentioned period." For an Indian applicant: "applicants traveling from outside Japan may commence their residency only on or after July 1." Closed for winter break 29 December 2027 to 3 January 2028, when "resident artists are required to temporarily vacate SCCP". Applicants must name three preferred periods, each a minimum of 60 days.

provides.grant: "For accepted Guest Artist, a maximum 200,000 yen, including tax incurred in Japan, will be funded. The payment will be made after SCCP receives the donated works mentioned in (5) below."
provides.stipend: No separate living stipend. The 200,000 yen honorarium is the only cash to the artist, and it is paid only after the donated work or technical information is handed over. "The cost of transportation, materials, shipping of works and luggage, and other living expenses are to borne by the residents."
provides.housing: Accommodation exists on site but the artist PAYS for it. "Twin Room: 26,400 yen per month (if preferred). Single Room: 20,300 yen per month (if preferred). Bedding Set: We will introduce a bedding supplier (e.g. 6,600 yen per month)." Air-conditioner use is billed on top, monthly and at the end of the stay.
provides.airfare: "Round-trip travel expenses from the accepted Guest Artist's location to Shigaraki Station will be reimbursed. However, in the case of overseas residents, the most economical round-trip travel expenses from your nearest airport to Shigaraki Station will be reimbursed."
provides.accommodation: No meals provided. Living expenses are the artist's own.
provides.workspace: SHARED, and open to public view. The guideline does not describe a private studio: "Please be aware that studio visitors who have completed registration may tour the studio during open hours at the SCCP." Studio hours 06:00 to 24:00; park open 09:30 to 17:00, closed Mondays.
provides.artist_fee: The 200,000 yen is described as funding tied to the donation of work, so it functions as a fee for the donated work rather than a living stipend. No other fee is named.
provides.materials: "The SCCP will cover the cost of materials required for creating up to a maximum of 100,000 yen. Any materials cost exceeding this limit will be at the Guest Artist's expense." Separately, firing: "The SCCP will cover the cost of kiln facility usage and fuel expenses up to a maximum of 110,000 yen. Any firing costs exceeding this limit will be at the Guest Artist's expense."

application_requirements.bio: "Biography (max.400 words)" in the English guideline; the Japanese guideline says 略歴（800字以内）, within 800 characters. The online form offers "Curriculum vitae (800 characters max, or separate PDF)".
application_requirements.website: Website and social media URLs are fields on the online form. Note: "Social media account information provided in the application materials will be linked on the SCCP website. If you do not wish for this information to be made public, you can leave it blank".
application_requirements.portfolio: "Majoy past works photos (up to 4 images)" (sic, in the official English guideline). Each work entry takes title, year, dimensions and an image. A portrait photo of the artist is also uploaded. Optional additional materials as a PDF. No references or letters are requested.
application_requirements.artwork_details: Per work: title, year, dimensions, image. The form also asks year ceramics practice began, museum exhibition count, juried exhibition acceptances, previous residency dates, techniques and processes used, grants or fellowships, and how the applicant heard about the programme.
application_requirements.image_count: Up to 4 work images, plus 1 portrait photo.
application_requirements.image_video_format: No video is accepted. "All image files, such as portraits and artwork photos, must be in JPEG format. Please ensure that the file size is below 2MB." Additional materials: PDF only, maximum 3.0 MB. Filename rule: "For all data, including portraits, artwork photos, PDF files, etc., please use only alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), underscores (_), and periods (.) in the file names."
application_requirements.submission_method: Online only, via the Guest Artist form at https://sccp-air-apply.jp/guest-artist/ . "We are accepting applications online. Please submit application via the link on the website... If you plan to apply for both Studio Artist and Guest Artist positions, please submit separate applications through the respective links." Application window 1 September 2026 10:00 JST to 31 October 2026 17:00 JST. No application fee is mentioned anywhere in the guideline. A confirmation email is sent on receipt; SCCP warns that Hotmail addresses have had delivery failures.
questions: Theme and concept of your works and production (max. 400 words)
Purpose and plan of your residency in the SCCP (max. 400 words)
When indicating your preferred residency period, please specify up to three residency period preferences.
Do you want to stay with accompaniers such as assistant. If so, write name, age, and if an assistant needs a separate room.
Please indicate any considerations you would like us to take into account in your participation.
other: LANGUAGE: an official English guideline exists for 2027, at https://www.sccp.jp/air-en/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/08/GA_application_guideline_2027_EN.pdf , and the online application form at sccp-air-apply.jp/guest-artist is bilingual Japanese and English with English field labels. The guideline does not state that the application must be written in Japanese, and English word limits are given, so English is acceptable. Confirm directly if in doubt.

Eligibility: "Applicants must be 20 years old or older at the time of application." "Priority will be given to ceramic artists and visual artists who have a clear motivation and purpose for undertaking a residency at SCCP, and who are expected to make a positive contribution to fellow Studio Artists in residence, as well as to the local ceramic community and ceramic industry."
Places: "Several artists (We expect to select one artist residing in Japan and one artist residing outside Japan.)" So realistically one international slot.

MANDATORY DONATION: "We kindly request that the Guest Artist donate the work(s) or technical information to Shiga Prefecture or the designated administrator. The selection of works for donation will be done through consultation with the SCCP staff. Please note that we may decline the donation request for large-scale works." The 200,000 yen is paid only after this.
MANDATORY PUBLIC PROGRAMME: "The Guest Artist will be expected to give a lecture or workshops, targeting to the general public."
Insurance: recommended for all; "Artists coming from outside Japan who will reside in Japan for four months or longer are required to enroll in the Japanese National Health Insurance program."
Everything must be removed at the end: "Please make sure to take all your artworks, materials, and personal belongings with you when your stay concludes."

Results notified by email by 27 December 2026. An 'Invitation Notice' and supporting documents are issued after schedule coordination, which is what a visa application would rely on. Arrive by 16:00 on day one.
Selection is on submitted materials alone: "The selection of Guest Artists will be based on the materials you submit. Please provide as much detail as possible."

SCCP invites pre-application contact: "we welcome inquiries from prospective Guest Artists, including any questions or requests related to studio visits." Put 'Artist-in-Residence Inquiry' in the subject line.

unconfirmed: Whether the studio is private or shared: the 2027 guideline never says. It only states that registered visitors may tour the studio during opening hours, which implies a viewable and likely shared space. Studio detail sits on https://www.sccp.jp/air-en/about-artist-in-r/ , not checked in this pass.
Visa support specifics for an Indian passport holder: the guideline mentions an 'Invitation Notice' issued after selection but says nothing about visa sponsorship, category or assistance.
Whether the 200,000 yen is taxed at source beyond the note "including tax incurred in Japan".

Word-limit conflict: the English guideline says 400 words for each of the three written sections, the Japanese guideline says 800 characters, and the live form says 800 characters. Work to the tighter reading or ask air.shigaraki@sccp.jp.

Whether non-ceramic mixed media and installation work is genuinely competitive: the call says "ceramic artists and visual artists" and the funded costs are materials and kiln firing, but no medium is formally excluded.
